summary: This document defines the data types and management policy for the IPFIX information model. The model is maintained as the IANA IPFIX Information Elements registry, with initial contents from RFC 5102. The IPFIX protocol uses it to encode measured traffic and related information.

plainLanguage.summary: IPFIX exports measurements about network traffic. RFC 7012 defines how each reported fact is named, described and typed, while the IANA registry holds the current list of facts.

questions: what is an ipfix information element
what data types does ipfix define
how are ipfix information elements registered
what does the post prefix mean in ipfix
subtitle: The shared definitions and rules behind the data elements used in IPFIX flow reports.

tldr.problem: The IPFIX protocol defines how to transmit information elements, but the protocol specification does not provide the full list of elements or the data types and management rules for them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7012 defines the properties, naming conventions, abstract data types, semantics and registry process for IPFIX Information Elements.
tldr.outcome: The IANA IPFIX Information Elements registry is the normative list of elements. RFC 7012 obsoletes RFC 5102.

today: RFC 7012 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2013. It obsoletes RFC 5102; the IANA IPFIX Information Elements registry is the normative list of elements.

sections.title: What the Information Model Defines
sections.content:
The IPFIX protocol, specified in RFC 7011, defines how Information Elements are transmitted and how basic data types are encoded. It does not define the complete list of elements that a report can contain, such as flow addresses, packet counts, observation points or sampling rates.

RFC 7012 describes the IPFIX information model and its data types. The complete list of Information Elements is maintained in the IANA IPFIX Information Elements registry, whose initial contents came from RFC 5102. The model does not define relationships among elements or a specific encoding.
sections.plainLanguage: A flow report needs agreed names and meanings for the facts it carries. This RFC sets the rules for those definitions; the IANA registry lists the individual facts.

sections.title: Required and Optional Element Properties
sections.content:
Every Information Element must define a unique name, numeric elementId, description, dataType and status. Status is either current or deprecated; newly defined elements have current status. Descriptions for constrained string or octet-array elements must state their length constraints.

Enterprise-specific elements also require an enterpriseId when they need to be globally unique outside the enterprise. Optional properties include data-type semantics, units, valid range and references. Registry entries also have a revision number, starting at 0, and a date for each revision.

Most elements have a scope in their definition. An Options Template can narrow that scope further with scope fields.
sections.plainLanguage: Each registry entry needs a name, number, explanation, type and status. It can also state units, allowed values, references and the date of a revision.

sections.title: Names and the Meaning of the post Prefix
sections.content:
Information Element names should describe the element and must be unique within the registry. Names begin with a lowercase letter. In a composed name, later parts begin with capitals, as in sourceMacAddress; enterprise-specific names should begin with a vendor name.

A name beginning with post describes a flow property after a middlebox has changed it. For example, an observation point before a packet marker may report ipClassOfService before the change and postIpClassOfService after it. The post value may come from another reliable source within the observation domain rather than direct observation at the observation point.
sections.plainLanguage: Element names follow a consistent spelling pattern. The prefix post means the reported value is from after a middlebox changed a flow property.

sections.title: Data Types and Their Semantics
sections.content:
The model defines abstract data types independently of how a protocol encodes them. Types include signed and unsigned integers, floating-point numbers, booleans, strings, octet arrays, addresses, timestamps and structured lists. IPFIX encoding for these types is defined separately in RFC 7011.

Numeric types can have additional semantics. quantity is the default measured value. totalCounter counts independently of export, while deltaCounter resets to zero each time it is exported or expires without export. An identifier is meaningful for equality comparison, and flags represents bit fields and must use an unsigned type.
sections.plainLanguage: A data type tells a collector what kind of value to expect, such as a number, address or time. A semantic label adds meaning, for example whether a number is a running counter or a value reset at export.

sections.title: Information Element Identifiers
sections.content:
IANA assigns identifiers in the range 1-32767. The range 1-127 is compatible with NetFlow version 9 field types for historical reasons. New elements generally receive the lowest available identifier from 128-32767.

Enterprise-specific identifiers use the same range and are paired with an enterprise identifier, so different enterprises can use the same element number without creating a collision. Identifier 0 is also reserved for enterprise-specific use.

The registry is the normative list of elements. The RFC retains a historical account of categories used in RFC 5102 but does not carry those categories into the registry.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA assigns a number to each shared element. An enterprise pairs its own number with an enterprise identifier so it can distinguish that element from another company's element.

sections.title: Adding and Revising Registry Entries
sections.content:
New Information Element definitions are added through Expert Review using the process in RFC 7013. Experts called IE-DOCTORS are appointed by the IESG. Identifiers from 1-127 may be assigned only to elements compatible with NetFlow version 9, as judged by a designated expert.

Changing or deprecating an element originally defined by an RFC requires IETF consensus. New abstract data types and semantics require Standards Action and must be defined in an IETF Standards Track document that updates RFC 7012. The RFC also describes registry revision and date fields.
sections.plainLanguage: Experts review requests before new elements enter the registry. Changes to elements defined by an RFC need IETF agreement, so users have a stable shared definition.

sections.title: Protecting Exported Information
sections.content:
The information model does not itself create security issues, but the data it describes may be sensitive for privacy or business reasons. Exported packet-header values can give the recipient information that would otherwise require direct observation of traffic on the data path.

The protocol that carries the information must therefore protect its integrity and confidentiality. RFC 7012 points to the IPFIX protocol specification, RFC 7011, for those procedures.
sections.plainLanguage: Flow reports can expose private or business-sensitive details. The protocol carrying them must protect the reports from changes and from people who should not read them.

items.text: Unique and meaningful in the registry.

items.title: Identifier
items.text: A numeric element ID, assigned by IANA.

items.title: Description
items.text: Explains the element's meaning and source.

items.title: Enterprise ID
items.text: Identifies enterprise-specific elements outside the enterprise.
